title: Governor of California

context.text: Open seat: Gov. Gavin Newsom (D) is term-limited. Under California's top-two primary system, the two highest vote-getters on June 2, 2026 advance regardless of party; Xavier Becerra (D) received 28% and Steve Hilton (R) 25%.
Hilton finished ahead of Democrat Tom Steyer, who spent more than $200 million of his own money in the primary and later urged supporters to back Becerra.

candidates.name: Xavier Becerra
candidates.ballotNote: Top-two primary finisher (28%); one of two candidates on the official certified general-election list. California governors have no ballot-line running mate; the lieutenant governor is elected separately.
candidates.currentRole: Former U.S. Secretary of Health and Human Services (2021–2025) and California Attorney General (2017–2021)

summary.text: Xavier Becerra is a Democrat and former California attorney general, U.S. Secretary of Health and Human Services and member of Congress (1993–2017). His campaign emphasizes lowering housing, utility and insurance costs and resisting Trump administration policies.

background.text: Born in Sacramento; B.A. in economics (1980) and J.D. (1984) from Stanford University.
Served in the California State Assembly (1990–1992) and the U.S. House of Representatives (1993–2017), including as chair of the House Democratic Caucus (2013–2017).
Appointed California Attorney General by Gov. Jerry Brown in 2017 and elected to a full term in 2018; U.S. Secretary of Health and Human Services under President Biden, 2021–2025.

priorities.text: Declare a state of emergency to freeze insurance and utility rates, and declare the housing shortage a state of emergency to fund the nearly 40,000 affordable housing units in approved projects that await a final tranche of funding.
Continue challenging Trump administration policies, as he did when he sued the administration more than 120 times as attorney general.
Expand state health coverage toward universal access and lower costs, including by eliminating duplicative healthcare oversight requirements.

positions.summary: Says that where zoning locks out affordable housing from entire communities he would open it up, and that his administration would pursue zoning reform and enforce the law on cities that shirk their housing obligations.
positions.quote: Where zoning still locks out affordable housing from entire communities, we will open it up.

positions.summary: Says California must protect coverage for every Californian and build toward universal access to health coverage.
positions.quote: We need to protect coverage for every Californian today while building toward a system where universal access is not a promise deferred but a guarantee delivered.

positions.summary: Calls the clean-energy transition necessary and urgent while saying climate action must be affordable, reliable and fair.
positions.quote: California’s clean-energy transition is necessary and urgent—but too many families are paying the price through rising utility bills, unreliable service, and confusing rate structures.

record.text: As California Attorney General, led a coalition of 20 states and D.C. in petitioning the U.S. Supreme Court to review the Fifth Circuit's decision in Texas v. U.S., which held the ACA's individual mandate unconstitutional.

candidates.name: Steve Hilton
candidates.ballotNote: Top-two primary finisher (25%); one of two candidates on the official certified general-election list; endorsed by President Donald Trump.
candidates.currentRole: Political commentator; former Fox News host

summary.text: Steve Hilton is a Republican political commentator who hosted 'The Next Revolution' on Fox News from 2017 to 2023 and was a policy adviser to UK Prime Minister David Cameron. His platform centers on income- and gas-tax cuts, loosening housing and environmental rules and changing the state's sanctuary law.

background.text: Born in London in 1969; studied Philosophy, Politics and Economics at New College, Oxford.
Served as director of strategy for UK Prime Minister David Cameron, 2010–2012; moved to California in 2012 and became a U.S. citizen in 2021.
Co-founded the crowd-funding platform Crowdpac and hosted Fox News's 'The Next Revolution' from 2017 to 2023.

priorities.text: Eliminate state income tax on the first $150,000 of earnings (income above that taxed at 8%) and lower gas prices, including by removing the state's 60-cent-per-gallon gasoline excise tax and reducing fuel regulations (his '$3 gas' plan).
Repeal wind and solar mandates and subsidies to cut electricity bills, and reduce regulation on housing construction.
Bring back the 'starter home' by reducing or deferring fees on entry-level homes, fast-tracking approvals and creating a state-backed starter home loan program for first-time buyers.

positions.summary: Says he would repeal California's wind and solar mandates and subsidies and let natural gas, nuclear and rooftop solar compete on a level playing field.
positions.quote: Steve Hilton will repeal California's costly wind and solar mandates and subsidies

positions.summary: His policy page says California has some of the most restrictive gun laws in the country and proposes an executive order directing state agencies to review their firearm policies for conflicts with the Second Amendment and recent Supreme Court rulings, plus a review of state firearm laws to identify restrictions he considers unconstitutional.
positions.quote: Instead of focusing on criminals who misuse firearms, Democrats in state government have targeted law abiding citizens with layer after layer of regulation.

positions.summary: His education plan says he would expand school choice through education savings accounts, starting with low-income and special-needs students, and bring back and expand the parent trigger law.
positions.quote: Hilton will expand choice through ESAs, starting with low-income and special needs students.

positions.summary: His plan would raise the California Highway Patrol's annual budget to $4 billion and build it toward 10,000 sworn officers, paid for by cutting executive-branch headcount.
positions.quote: Steve will increase CHP’s annual budget to $4 billion and build the force toward 10,000 sworn officers.

positions.summary: At a March 2026 town hall he said “sanctuary policies will end” and that his administration would partner with the federal government on enforcement (per The Santa Barbara Independent); in a September 30, 2026 Deadline interview he described working within the sanctuary state law and focusing removals on people who have committed crimes.
positions.quote: work together within the sanctuary state law to focus on removing the people who most Californians would agree shouldn’t be here

statements.quote: move us toward life in ways that are achievable and realistic
statements.context: At a March 2026 Santa Barbara town hall, per The Santa Barbara Independent, which also reports he would oppose public funds for out-of-state abortion travel

statements.quote: Steve Hilton will cap the combined cost of fees, permits and government mandates at $50,000 per new home, cut the rules and delays that make building so expensive, and open up more places for starter homes.
statements.context: On his campaign policy page on new-home fees

statements.quote: But more spending is not success if families still cannot afford care, and an insurance card is not much use if nobody will take it.
statements.context: On his Working Class Healthcare Guarantee policy page, which proposes price transparency, more providers and changes to Medi-Cal

candidates.researchNotes: Positions and statements come from campaign policy pages (rendered in headless Chromium and matched verbatim), a March 2026 Santa Barbara Independent report of a town hall, and a September 30, 2026 Deadline interview. His immigration position is shown as mixed because his March and September remarks differ in emphasis. A Fox News video headline quoting him on transgender athletes was not used because the page text did not include his words in context. No statement found on rent regulation, minimum wage, tariffs, taxes on high earners or war powers.

researchNotes: The California Secretary of State's Official Certified List of Candidates for the November 3, 2026 general election (dated August 27, 2026) lists exactly two governor candidates, Xavier Becerra (Democratic) and Steve Hilton (Republican); this matches the guide. Ballotpedia was unreachable (bot challenge). Issue positions and candidate quotes come from the campaign issue pages, which were rendered in headless Chromium and matched verbatim against page text. A record item citing an HHS statement was removed because its archived page no longer loads and the official HHS page could not be retrieved. Becerra's House voting record and Hilton's campaign website content were not reviewed in depth. Running mates: California elects the lieutenant governor separately.
